positive_experience.text: Repeated requests for labs, CXR, or imaging without prior targeted history or physical exam yield no useful evidence; prioritize symptom-focused questioning before ordering diagnostic tests.

Requesting labs or CXR in this case was ineffective because no results were available and the diagnosis was resolved through history and symptom pattern; avoid redundant tool requests when clinical history and targeted questions already support a diagnosis.

Gradual worsening of shortness of breath from exertion to rest, combined with cough producing yellow sputum and frequent albuterol use, strongly supports asthma exacerbation in an elderly patient; do not apply this pattern if symptoms are acute, systemic, or associated with trauma or joint pain.

Elderly patients with GI bleeding often present without hematemesis; relying solely on classic signs like hematemesis misses a significant proportion of upper GI bleeds, especially in this demographic.
Black tarry stools and coffee-ground vomiting strongly suggest upper gastrointestinal bleeding; this pattern is highly specific and should prompt immediate diagnostic workup even without hematemesis.

negative_experience.text: Pelvic pressure, urinary urgency, and dyspareunia in a patient with a pelvic mass raise suspicion of malignancy, but absence of weight loss, fatigue, or night sweats does not rule it out; these symptoms are not specific to benign leiomyoma and should not be used to dismiss malignancy without imaging or biopsy.

Abdominal cramping pain, constipation followed by diarrhea with mucus, syncope, and lightheadedness in an elderly female with no fever or blood in stool should prompt consideration of colorectal cancer, especially when fatigue and itching are present; do not assume diverticulitis without weight loss or typical RLQ tenderness.

Fever, fatigue, weight loss, confusion, and tachypnea in an elderly patient strongly suggest systemic infection or malignancy; do not apply this pattern when symptoms are localized, acute, or accompanied by clear infectious signs like cough or purulent discharge.
